utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. Case number IT-95-9-T, the Prosecutor versus Blagoje Simic, Milan Simic, Miroslav Tadic, and Simo Zaric.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. We are ready for cross-examination of the witness. Can the witness be brought into the courtroom. The proceedings have been delayed because the courtroom was not cleared on time. So that's why we are sitting late.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Witness, you are reminded that you are still under solemn declaration. So you may sit down.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Who will begin? Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good day, Mr. Dagovic. I am Dragan Krgovic, and I am defence attorney for Mr. Miroslav Tadic, and I'm going to ask you several questions. My questions will be formulated in such a way that your answer could be yes or no. If you are not sure or don't know something, you can say so. You can say, "I don't know" or "I am not sure." I will try to ask such questions which will lead you to state the correct answer, since both of us are speaking the same language, the Trial Chamber has to wait for the interpretation to be finished. So I would kindly request that you make a small pause after I ask my question, wait for the interpretation to be finished and then begin your answer so that we could make the whole procedure easier and quicker. Thank you. In your statement before this Tribunal in November, you spoke about the AS Cafe, and you mentioned that the Cafe AS was a place where members of the 4th Detachment used to meet. Is that true?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Would you agree with me or do you know if members of other ethnic groups also frequented the AS Cafe, just like they did frequent other cafes and restaurants? So was it visited by members of the Croat and Muslim ethnicities?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I just wanted to say that yes, those members were also members of the same paramilitary units, just like the gentlemen who are sitting here.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: You're thinking of the 4th Detachment?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The 4th Detachment and other members of the special forces.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know that Sulejman Tihic, president of the SDA of Bosanski Samac and the current president of the SDA of Bosnia and Herzegovina also used to come to the AS Cafe?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, if he did, I don't know. He probably used to come there before the war as well, but I don't know about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know whether Alija Fitozovic also came to the AS and he was the Chief of Staff of the newly formed TO?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If he did, I'm not familiar with that. And perhaps he also used to frequent the cafe before the war.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know that Izet Izetbegovic, the vice-president of the SDA and a cousin of -- or a nephew of Alija Izetbegovic also used to come to this cafe?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I think the same applies to them as to the other two people that we talked about.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Before -- I mean, before the conflict broke out. Immediately before.

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it's something that I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know that Hasan Bicic, the owner of the pizzeria where you worked used to come to the pizzeria before the war and immediately before the outbreak of the conflict?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Before the war, yes. But immediately before the outbreak of the hostilities, I don't believe that he came, because that's probably something that I would know. Before the war, yes, perhaps.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Counsel, I think we need a clarification. We've got coming to the pizzeria, presumably --

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Did he come to the Cafe AS? Please clarify this because of the transcript. When I asked about Mr. Hasan Bicic, whom I indicated was the owner of the pizzeria where you worked. So the question was: Did he come to the AS Cafe? So your anxious, does that -- is that in relation to the -- his visiting of the Cafe AS?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, perhaps he did used to come before, but he didn't get there immediately -- visit there before the outbreak of the hostilities.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: But did you ever go to the Cafe AS?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I never did, and I'm glad that I never did.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: I would like to remind counsel and the witness, please, to pause. After the question, the witness should wait, watch the screen. When the mouse has stopped, then start answering. Because it's one person interpreting the question and the answer. So please do pause.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. I will pay attention to that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know that the headquarters of the 4th Detachment was situated at the Sit factory across the street from the AS Cafe.

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, amongst other things.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: We will move to another topic that you also talked about during your testimony on the 9th of November, 2001. On page 3990 in your statement, you mention that when you used to go to town, you would see Miroslav Tadic there in uniform. Is this true?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: You used to see Mr. Tadic just in passing, I assume. You didn't speak to him.

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: And that was a few days or a couple of days after the 17th of April, if I understood you properly.

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This was before the 17th of April, and it was also after the 17th of April. So they patrolled the town in uniform before the war.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Miroslav Tadic or members of the 4th Detachment?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Miroslav Tadic and also Mr. Zaric and members of the 4th Detachment.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: In uniform?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In uniform.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Was this a uniform of the JNA?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, these were camouflage uniforms. The JNA no longer existed there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: You're talking about the period before the 17th of April that the JNA didn't exist.

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, you know that Bosnia was recognised as a state. You know the dates. So with that date, the JNA no longer existed on that territory.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Was this a uniform that was used by the JNA previously?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Since they inherited everything from the former JNA, yes, this was the former JNA uniform.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Each time that you saw him, was Miroslav Tadic in uniform, as well as immediately after the 17th of April?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. He wasn't in uniform every time. Excuse me, I just wanted to say this: Before -- when I saw him before the 17th of April, he wasn't in uniform each time. But when I used to see him after the 17th of April, and I saw him a couple of times, he was wearing a uniform.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: When you saw him on the 17th of April, after the 17th of April how long -- what was the time frame? Was that a couple of days later? Or how many days?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it -- I'm not -- I don't know exactly. It was a couple of days later.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Was -- when Miroslav Tadic was there during your exchange, was he wearing a uniform at that time?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: What kind of uniform?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Camouflage.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: The same kind of uniform that you used to see him in before?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know if it was the same uniform, but it looked the same.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: You were exchanged at the UNPA zone.

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: The other participants in the exchange, were they also wearing uniforms?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. But I would like to add that at the time of the exchange in Dragalic, Mr. Tadic was not wearing a uniform, meaning that when we stopped before the bridge in Bosanska Gradiska, perhaps he took his uniform off. He changed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: I asked you about the exact time of the exchange.

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. But during the trip to the place of exchange, he was wearing a uniform.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: In your statement before the Trial Chamber on the 9th of November, 2001, you described an event which took place on the 28th of October, 1992, when your uncle, Ahmed Vukovic was killed. And you mentioned at that time that he was killed by a shell. Is that true?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: The shell which killed your uncle was fired from the territory of the Republic of Croatia; is that true?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: The MUP building where you were detained was in the centre of Bosanski Samac; is that true?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Next to it is the municipal building; is that true?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: And there are housing apartments all around, residential buildings all around it; is that true?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: How do you know that the shell which hit the MUP did not come from the Croatian side?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Since you're talking about this, I hope that you were at the place where this tragedy or this crime took place. So if you look at the side from which the shell came from, it came from the direction of Obudovac, from Zabari, so that's not Croatia. If you look at the side that it fell from, unless the grenade -- the shell happened to twist during its flight. The other thing is that they knew in Croatia that detainees were being held there, so they probably would not be the ones who would target the MUP.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: That place was at that time under the Croat control, under the HVO control.

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Who was controlling that place?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Serb paramilitary forces were controlling it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Weiner.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: He's said now twice "that place." What are we referring to at this point?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Okay. You want clarification.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: In his question, "that place at that time was under Croat control." and "who was controlling that place?"

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. You want counsel to -- yes. I'm sure counsel has understood the query by Mr. Weiner to clarify the venue being referred to.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: So you know where the -- that time the shells which fell on Samac came from, that time when your uncle was killed.

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you look at the scene of the crime, the shell came from Obudovac and Zabari. Zabari and Obudovac. Who controlled that place?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At that time, and it still is under the control of Serb paramilitary forces.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: How far is that place from the MUP building?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Between 8 and 10 kilometres, as the crow flies. Perhaps less.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: So this is within range of the weapons which caused the death of your uncle --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Before he answers that, I object to that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Weiner.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: They're now asking him about the range of certain types of weapons. If they're going to have him answer concerning the types of weapons, whether it's mortars or whatever type of artillery, there should be some indication that he has qualifications to offer those opinions or conclusions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, counsel.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I respond? Your Honours, as long as -- on page 3998 in his statement of the 9th of November, he talked about him serving in the army and how he heard the sound of the shell and how he's very familiar with the weapon that caused the death of his uncle and that he knows what it -- it is like to fire from such a weapon. In view of all of that, that's the only reason why I'm asking that question. If my learned friend Mr. Weiner agrees, I can perhaps read from the witness's statement of the 9th of November.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: With that explanation?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: If they want to concede that he's qualified, I'll let him answer questions concerning artillery.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. I'm sure the witness will be able to answer if he doesn't know-

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Yes. I can.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Could you please answer, then.

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, of course. If you read my statement carefully, you would have seen that I said that not that time when the shell fell -- I didn't say what the millimetres of that shell was. I said that it was VBR, so when Samac was shelled, you could tell -- you could differentiate between the shells fired from a mortar, from a gun, or from another weapon. But perhaps if you need further information, you'd better ask the army that actually did the shelling. They would give you better information.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: When your uncle was killed, did you happen to recognise the sound, and so could you tell which weapons the shell was fired from?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: So which weapon was that?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It was a VBR, it was a multi-rocket launcher -- multiple rocket launcher.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: From your statement, if I understood it properly, it seems that Serbs shelled Bosanski Samac, which happened to be under their control. Did I understand you properly?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. But I would also like to say something important on top of what you have said, whether this was done intentionally or accidentally. But each time that Samac was shelled, I -- the camps -- because there were several locations where they would shell -- at that time, they would ask us detainees would we take the rifles from the 4th Detachment, from the Serbian army, and then they would accompany that by saying, "So you see, your own side is killing you." So I think that this was an intentional plan, or a strategy, just like everything else was.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: During that period of shelling, the shelling was daily -- Bosanski Samac was shelled daily.

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The town of Bosanski Samac itself wasn't shelled daily, but the environs were.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Counsel, please remember to pause.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SINGH
utterances.text: Incidentally, was this the shell that landed on the top of the police station where your uncle was on the roof?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. The shell fell on the roof of the garage where my uncle was. So this was in the yard of the MUP building.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Were civilian targets in Samac also shelled?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, as far as I know, there was shooting. I know that the Croatian side shelled. They wanted to hit the 4th Detachment HQ, but they happened to hit a private house in that part. As far as I was able to see from the camp, that's what I'm able to talk about. But I don't know what was happening in town.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: So there was shelling by the Croatian side.

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Absolutely.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Frequently?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not so frequently.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: As frequently as there was shelling from the Serb side?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I'm saying it again: Croatia shelled areas under Serb control that were outside of the town of Samac frequently, but they also shelled the town of Samac itself. But as far as I know, on that occasion, the shelling came from an area that was under the control of the Serbian army.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: So as far as I understood you, Croats would shell the outskirts of Samac and sometimes the city, while the Serbs shelled exclusively the centre of town, where you had the police station, the TO, and other facilities where detainees were kept. So this is your statement, if I've understood you properly.

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the way you put it, it appears as if this happened hundreds of times. But actually, the SUP was shelled twice, and the TO, so this was during the time that I was detained. I don't know what you mean, did they do the same things as the Croats or the Serbs. I'm not sure exactly what you mean.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: As far as I know, the VBR has 16 shells which can be fired at the same time, and the firing is very concentrated. So what I would like to know is where the other shells fell on that occasion when the garage of the SUP -- of the MUP was hit.

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, who could tell? Perhaps the VBR at that time was loaded with only two shells instead of 16.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: I'm only asking you whether any other shell exploded on that occasion.

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that at that time, close to the SUP, in the immediate vicinity of the SUP, one house was hit or a courtyard of a house close to the SUP and that also, something was also hit close to the Red Cross building. So we're talking about two or three shells, and not 16.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: So when you fire one or two shells, then, this is a mortar, because a multiple rocket launcher cannot fire only two or three. But perhaps you know better.

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I know a little more than you obviously, because a VBR can be loaded also with a couple of shells.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: On that occasion, when the SUP was shelled, you mentioned one man who was there right away, and he was sorry about all of the things that were destroyed in that garage that was hit.

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: What was his name -- what was the name of that man?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The name of that man was Pero Krstanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: He arrived immediately after the hit.

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I'm sorry, I just wanted to correct something. It says "Stanovic" here, but it was Krstanovic, so it was not said properly.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Well, the interpretation or the Translation Unit will correct the transcript later. So this person was there immediately after?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, not -- not immediately after, but after a few minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: The shelling of the SUP, where were the Serbs who were guarding you, the prison guards, the staff who was -- were working in MUP, the police officers?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, mostly they were in the yard, and they were in the SUP building, in the camp building.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I would now like to tender a map. This is a detailed town map of the town of Samac. During the break, we received this from the land survey department of Bosanski Samac. It is more detailed than the maps we have had so far. It also includes the names of streets and buildings at the time when these events were taking place, namely, during the years of war, 1991, 1992. The OTP is welcome to use this map as well, and I imagine that they will not object to its admission.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. Weiner, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Could I have a few moments to look at it, or could we mark it for ID at this time? I've never seen it before. I don't think there's any problem with it, I --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Oh, you just want to study it for a few moments.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Yes. I just want to study it. That's all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: All right. Can we have it marked for identification, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours. It's D27/3 ter ID.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, counsel. You can proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Dagovic, have you seen this map?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: I mean right now. Right now have you seen it, just now.

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Oh, yes. Now I have, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: What does it seem like to you? Does it actually depict the streets and the buildings as they were in 1991, 1992, in Bosanski Samac?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: To be quite frank, it all seems very vague to me. I can barely see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Take a look at the actual map, rather than the monitor.

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Oh, yes. I see. Well, I see two names here, one is Ive Lole Ribara the other is Rasima Halilovica, so this confuses me.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: This is probably the name that came later. So we are talking about the old names in this case?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it seems all right as far as I can see at this point.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Can you show us on this map where the building of the MUP is where you were detained.

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Right here.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: You can take the marker that is in front of you, and could you please put a circle round it.

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May it please be recorded that the witness showed the location of the MUP building on this map.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: By a red circle.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, red circle.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Can you show us on this map where the River Sava is and the boundary with the Republic of Croatia.

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the Sava River, and this is where the boundary is. This is where Croatia is, over here.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Can you just put a little mark there that's closest to the line.

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What do you mean?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Can you put a little cross by the Sava River and the boundary with Croatia.

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Counsel, the river surely has to be taken into consideration when one's determining the boundary. This cross, I think, clearly identifies where the land territory of Croatia starts. But if we're talking, obviously, in international boundary terms, we have to presumably take the median line, which is the usual delimitation point of the river.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May the record reflect that the witness marked the bank on the Croatian territory with a little cross, that is to say, on the opposite bank of the Sava River.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Fine.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: May I ask you to put number "1" next to the MUP marking and number "2" next to the other mark that you made. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks] Can I say something? You said that this was a town map. I don't think so. This was just drawn by hand. Somebody did this. If you know, Samac, and I do, and I can see this better than you can, the cinema building is not here. Look at this little point here that I put.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's not here. It's somewhere around here approximately. Around here. That is to say, on the other side of the street. And at the place where the cinema is marked here, that is where the veterinarian community is, rather, where the veterinarians lived. This is the street of Edvard Kardelj, that is the street where the AS Cafe was. And this is the street Pero Bosic, that is to say, my street, so this is where the veterinarian community is and this is where the fire brigade is. See, here? And the cinema, therefore, and not there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: So you are only challenging the cinema location; right?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, as far as I could see. Perhaps there are other things also that aren't right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: I consulted Mr. Pisarevic after your objection, and Mr. Pisarevic says that perhaps you have confused things a bit, perhaps you are viewing it from the other side?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Pisarevic knows the town of Samac as well as I do, so perhaps he can I can --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Weiner.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: If Pisarevic was would like to testify, that's fine. We're getting off base here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. I was wondering who was under cross-examination and who was counsel.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Actually, counsel, you said that this map is an official survey map?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Of the land surveying department which enters various buildings and maps and the land survey register, the land register.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: I was waiting for the interpretation to finish, because I have another question, which is: If this is an official survey map, I see no -- we're talking about stamps or whatever. There's no name as to the organisation that produced it or the date, the usual things that you would see on an official survey.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, we got this map from our investigator. And if necessary, we are going to get an official certificate with a stamp on it. The explanation we got was that this map was done after the land survey was completed and that it does depict the situation as it is viewed from aircraft and that names of streets and buildings are included from the period 1991/1992, and then also the amended street names are included as well. We will do our best to obtain a certified copy of this same map.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can I say something at this point?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have the map in front of me. I've had it for five minutes now. I found another mistake. I find this a bit unclear. How can this be a town map when -- look at this here. This is where the pensioner's home is. That's not correct either. The pensioner's home is somewhere around here, not here. So this entire town map is not very good. Look at the medical centre. It is here. If you look at the street of Edvard Kardelj, this is where the Cafe AS would be, Mr. Tadic's cafe, and then the medical centre would be here in relation to Cafe AS, not here. Or rather, the pensioner's home also would be here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: So the witness appears to be disputing the map as it is shown. So counsel?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I tendered this map, and I saw this on the actual spot, the Cafe AS and the cinema, especially the position of the Cafe AS. It's exactly the way it's depicted on this map. Of course, I cannot challenge the witness now. If he doesn't think that the map is authentic, that is his position. But we are going to provide a certified document concerning the authenticity of this map.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I hope that my -- that the next question I will be answering has to do with the shelling. You were going to tell me how a shell could have come from Obudovac when Obudovac is in such and such a place. So all of this doesn't fit together at all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Witness, just wait. Let's resolve this problem of the map. Yes, I can see Mr. Lukic on his feet.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, during the break, during the Christmas break, I obtained this map and I personally handed it over to Mr. Di Fazio about a month ago, and he said that he would check out this map through his own investigators and that we would receive information accordingly. I indeed have spent a great deal of time in Samac. I think that this map will be far more useful for all of us in these proceedings, more useful than the map that we have been using until now. And also, for these proceedings, it includes some very important building. I can agree with the witness concerning the cinema, but then I don't have to agree on that either. However, with regard to the key buildings in Samac, I think this map is much, much better than the map that we had been using and which was a Prosecution exhibit. We would, anyway like to tender this map and then perhaps the OTP through its own investigators can check this out and then they can say officially whether they object to this map or not. I repeat that at the beginning of January, I handed this map over to Mr. Di Fazio. Perhaps we can also take advantage of the witness's presence here, and we can refer to some of the locations that we had been referring to during these proceedings. For example, where the memorial is and places like that, then the medical centre. I think it is before the stadium, not after the stadium, like the witness has said. But of course, I'm not going to enter a polemic with the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Counsel, you're not going to give evidence. I'm sure we all know how to get a correct map from the relevant authorities for use for proceedings in court. Yes. So let's deal with the problem properly, rather than you arguing with the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I fully agree.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Weiner, the counsel has said this copy was given to the Prosecution?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: I didn't receive it. I will check with Mr. Di Fazio at the break. I've never seen it before. However, to move things along, I have no objection to having this marked for identification, which it has been, and using it as long as the witness agrees to the buildings represented in the map. If the witness agrees to certain buildings, let's just go ahead and use it and move this proceeding along, rather than sitting here and argue over admissibility at this point. Let's just --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. That's what -- that's what I wanted to hear from you. Because it's the witness who's being asked, and the witness has said he's familiar with the town. And if the witness says that as depicted this is wrong, he will put his own mark. And counsel doesn't have to argue with that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We have fully understood your instructions, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: And as we have been promised, the certified copy -- because this is a photostat copy. Yeah. So the proper map will be produced at later stage, so the proceedings can go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Dagovic, let's go back to the shelling. If I have understood you correctly, when you spoke about the shelling of Samac, those two times, you claim that the SUP building and the buildings around the SUP building were shelled by the Serb forces.

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I am convinced of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Can you show us on this map where the direction of Obudovac is.

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Obudovac is somewhere in this direction, around here.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Could you please put an arrow in red in that direction.

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: And could you please put down the approximate distance.

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know the distance. I'm not a land surveyor.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Approximately.

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, 8 to 10 kilometres as the crow flies. I don't know. Perhaps a bit more, perhaps a bit less.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Can we also have that arrow marked "3". It's easier to follow the map when you know what 1 is, what 2 is, what 3 is.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: So the shelling of Samac, let us conclude this subject. There were frequent shellings. In your opinion, a few times the Serbs from Obudovac shelled Samac. That was under their authority, namely, the MUP building where at the time of the shelling, as you had said, detainees were as well as persons who are ethnic Serbs. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sir, again, you keep saying "a few times." I said "twice." When -- twice is twice. And when you say "several times," I mean about ten times. I know about these two times. And that is when the SUP was hit and the TO building, or rather, that is what they were targeting. I said that the surroundings places were shelled. That is to say, where the Serb military was.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: And then on that occasion, both times at the TO building, at the SUP building, that's where Serb policemen were, people who were guarding you; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Dagovic, we are now going to move on to another subject. We won't be needing the map any more.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. You can remove it now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SINGH
utterances.text: Witness, may I just seek clarification from you. Can you give us your main reason clearly why you think the shells came from Obudovac.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, if you look at the direction, that is to say, where the shell came from, you can see that it came from the direction of Obudovac. Croatia is not in that direction. Croatia is on the right-hand side. So I put this arrow there, and that is where the shelling came from. The roof of the garage and the door of the garage, it came from Obudovac, not from Croatia. Had it come from Croatia, it would have hit the left-hand side.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Dagovic --

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, Judge Singh, have you completed your question? May I proceed now?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SINGH
utterances.text: I was just going to follow up the last sentence of his answer. Had it come from Croatia, it would have hit the left-hand side. Left-hand side of what, please?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Of the garage. Sir, I don't know where you are now in respect of the garage. If you are viewing the garage from the yard, then it's on the right-hand side. If you are looking from the garage towards the yard, then it's the left-hand side. And it hit the door, or rather, above the door. It hit the roof, that is to say, the part between the door and the roof of the garage. Only if the shell twisted as it was falling, which is highly unlikely.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Dagovic, let us go back to this subject. Is the territory of the Republic of Croatia to the right of Obudovac?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It depends on the direction that you're viewing it. If you're viewing it from the direction of Serbia, then that's the way it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: From the direction of Obudovac.

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I would like the witness to be shown D14/1 ter. That is the map of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina where the surroundings of Samac can be seen. And then the witness can show us some locations on this map.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us where Bosanski Samac is on this map.

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I can see here it is, Samac.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Can you put a circle around this in red. Please use the magic marker and put a number "1" there, please.

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, can this map be used? This is D14/1 ter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: It's already in evidence, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: It depends what you want to use it for. Because if it's marked by another witness, then we may get confused. So it's very important that you clarify how you're going to use it so that we don't get confused with other markings already on the map.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Weiner.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Your Honour, since there are other markings, can he place his initials by the circle he drew so we know which is his circle or the -- as opposed to the other circles which are down to the left of the picture, down towards the bottom. There's three other circles here on the map already.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'll put my initials there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: All right, Mr. Weiner?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Thank you, very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May the record reflect that the witness marked Bosanski Samac on this map, "1 ED."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Can you show us Obudovac on this map.

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Could you please mark that.

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: With a number "2"?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, and your initials.

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May the record reflect that the witness marked with the number "2" on this map the village of Obudovac, on this map.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Dagovic, if I remember correctly, you said that you were at the front line, that you were carrying sandbags, digging trenches. Can you show us on this map where the front line actually was at that time.

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you read carefully what I said, I did carry sandbags in the town of Samac. I was carrying them to the Silo in Samac, actually, and I put them on the embankment by the town of Samac. That is the one facing the River Bosna. That is to say, that I did not go any further, to any further front lines, that is.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know where the front line was at that time? Can you show it on the map?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know where the front line was. I was in a camp. I was not at the front line.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know where the boundary with Croatia was at that time?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Where it is now.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Can you please mark it.

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. So this would be the boundary with Croatia.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Could you please mark it with a red line.

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can, but it's marked already.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Because it's along the boundary of the River Sava, isn't it? The witness has said it is as it is shown on the map. So he doesn't have to mark it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Then there's no need for this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May the record reflect, though, that the witness did show on the map where the boundary is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yeah, he was showing along the River Sava.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Could you show us where Grebnice is.

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Approximately. I can't see Grebnice on the map. But let me take a closer look. If Orasje is there, then Grebnice would be somewhere around here. So I will put a dot there. So -- and I marked it with the number "3," so this is where Grebnice would be.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] For the transcript, I would like to note that the witness marked the place where Grebnice is, and he marked it with "3 ED."

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know this is where the confrontation line was between the Army of the Republika Srpska and the HVO?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I heard that. But it's important. I would like to add to that. I can indicate exactly where the line was. Because at that time the Serbian paramilitary forces had control all the way practically up to Orasje. They were practically at Orasje.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: When I asked you a while ago to tell us where the front line was, you said that you didn't know. And that's why I didn't go on about that.

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: But you were talking about Grebnice. Now we're talk about Grebnice. But Orasje is something else. Because when I was exchanged, I was at Orasje.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Weiner.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would ask that when they ask about the front line, instead of saying at that time, where was the front line at a certain time. Are we talking about April, May, June, or are we talking about while he was doing forced labour? Prior to his arrest? After his arrest?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Okay. You want a time specified.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Yes. Because this was a fluid-type situation. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I said at the beginning that when I'm talking about the front line, I'm talking about the shelling and I'm talking about the time that the bomb fell, which caused the death of the witness's uncle. So I'm talking about that time exclusively, the time period in October 1992.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation].

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: In October, 1992, Grebnice was on the front line; is that true?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes that's what I heard.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you know who was in control in Grebnice?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. That's where the front was, the front line. So nobody could be in control if that's where the front line was.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: So the forces of the Croatian Defence Council were at Grebnice on that line; is that true?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Probably. If that's where the front was, that's where they probably were.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We won't be needing the map any more.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Dagovic, in your statement from November 2001, on pages 4005 and 4006, you mentioned that you gave statements at -- to investigators at the SUP in Bosanski Samac; is this true?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This happened on several occasions.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Who did you give these statements to?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Amongst others, I gave a statement to Milos Savic and Vlado Sarkanovic. When I say amongst others, I mean that I also gave statements to the Serbian special forces.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: I'm interested in these statements given at the MUP to these two people that you have just mentioned.

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: So I've already said that Sarkanovic, Milos Savic, and the Serb specials. And all the statements were given at the SUP.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: While you were giving a statement to Milos Savic and Sarkanovic, were you treated decently by them? Were they decent to you?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What do you mean by that, did they treat me decently?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Did they apply force while you were giving your statement? Did they use force?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Savic and Sarkanovic did not use force, but immediately prior to giving the statement and after giving the statement, we would usually be beaten, and then we would have to give subsequent statements. So if the first statement was not deemed satisfactory, we would be beaten, and then would be expected to provide another statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: How many times did you provide statements to Savic and Sarkanovic?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I -- maybe -- several times. Perhaps three or four times. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Did you sign these statements, as far as you can recall?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I can recall, I signed three blank statements, three empty pieces of paper, and three written statements.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I would like to introduce into evidence the statements by this witness provided to the MUP, as well as an additional statement given at the MUP also in Bosanski Samac. One statement was given on the 28th of May -- the 8th of May, 1992, and the additional statements or supplementary statement was given on the 21st of October, 1992.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: I take it the copies -- the Prosecution have copies?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] To be precise, we obtained these statements from the Prosecution. Your Honours, I see that the witness has notes in front of him, as well as some papers, and I think that this is not permitted, so I would like to request that the witness not be permitted to use such notes, and could he please hand them over to the Trial Chamber.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I have some evidence here, but it's not a problem. I will hand them over.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: He doesn't have to hand them over. He should keep them away.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I didn't know, Your Honours, that I was -- I am not permitted to use this, and I will put all these papers to one side. And I apologise.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Perhaps the Prosecution can look at these pieces of evidence, and perhaps he can pass them on to us if this is evidence that the witness has prepared.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: He has put them away. He has explained that he was not aware that he can use papers. He has put them away.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Dagovic, could you please look at the first statement --

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Oh, I apologise. I would like to get an ID number, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: When you say the first statement, can you just elaborate, dated, record on such and such a place, for purposes of the record, so that we know which document we are dealing with.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The first statement was recorded on the 8th of May, 1992, in Bosanski Samac at the public security station. It's marked by the Prosecution, the English version, 00697113; and the B/C/S version is marked 00532786.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Counsel, we have received a statement. One is dated 8th May -- interviewed on 8th May 1992. That's the one you want to discuss with the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The 8th of May, yes. Yes, that's the date of the statement. If the Prosecution doesn't have any objections, we could tender that now so that then there would be no need to give it an ID number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. Weiner.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Your Honour, it's -- you have to introduce the statement through the witness. I have to see what the witness is going to say about it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Oh, because he hasn't yet asked him whether that is his statement. All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Dagovic, have you seen this statement?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I have.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Could you please tell me if this is the statement that you provided on the 8th of May, 1992 to investigators at the Bosanski Samac SUP.

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is part of the statement that I gave.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Could you please tell me if there is a signature on this statement of yours.

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Was the statement recorded or dictated in your presence, this partial statement, as you call it?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I was just going to say why I called it a partial statement. If you notice, if the Trial Chamber would like to notice, every -- the first part of the statement contains the true version of events, and the second part contains a version of events that I did not state. It's true that I signed the statement, but this second part of the text was not part of that statement at that time, because as far as I know, I never talked about Ibrahim called Ibela or Latif Rakitic. And if you may recall, I already said that I also signed blank statements. So they could have done whatever they wanted.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Do you remember signing this statement?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've just told you now, I never mentioned Ibela Salkic or Atic. And each they are mentioned in the second half of the statement and not the first half of the statement. So I think that this was added on later.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Is it true what it says here in the statement?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I've just told you now I would agree with you about -- partially about the first part of the statement, but I would definitely not agree with you on the second part of the statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: And can we just have an ID number before we forget. Can we mark it for identification purposes only.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours. This document, the English version is document D28/3 ID, and the B/C/S version is D28/3 ter ID.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: I wonder whether we could clarify what the witness means by "the first part of the statement" and "the second part of the statement," because as we see it, there are four paragraphs in it. So could we know which paragraphs he says are his and which paragraphs he's contesting -- contending or not, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, if we take the statement from the 8th of May, perhaps I would agree. I would agree with the first two paragraphs and not with the last two. So if you look at it, I am denying everything. And then at the end, I seem to accept everything, that there was -- it's mentioned here that some two months before, I had spoken to Atic, and it's obvious that this has been added on. And you can see the same thing when you look at it yourself. In the first part, I don't admit to anything. And then in the second part, I seem to be admitting to things. So perhaps it would have been better if I had just admitted to things in the first part right away.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's time for a break. Should we go on that break now and then continue after?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. We'll take our break as usual and continue at 14.15 [sic].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: The cross-examination is continuing with Mr. Krgovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Dagovic, we stopped for the break while -- when we were discussing the statements. The statement that you provided at the MUP on the 8th of May, 1992 and the first part that you say is your statement is correct.

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Up to which part do you think?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Up until the part that you're contesting.

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Excuse me, counsel. Sorry, the same point I raised before when I mentioned that they looked as though there were four paragraphs. I was look at the B/C/S text then. But now reading it in English, I see that there are -- it's been subdivided to a greater extent so, it's not simply four paragraphs. Would there be some way to maybe get the witness to indicate in reading it the point where the part that he says is correct ends and -- just to make it clear for us.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: You've heard the Trial Chamber. Could you please read out the last sentence indicating the last part of the part that's correct.

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It ends: "I did not agree to the -- I did not attend the meetings of the party, neither did I pay the membership dues."

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Dagovic, when you were giving that statement, the first part that you've read and that you're not contesting, this is what you told the investigators during the interrogation.

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: And the statement that you gave, you say that that is the statement that you have in front of you right now.

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Why did you sign the statement if this second part is not correct?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because this was added on to my statement once I had signed it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Could you please read the last part of this statement, the last paragraph.

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would like to clarify, because I can see that we're not understanding each other. When I was providing the answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: I would just like you to answer my question.

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. But you are making me -- leading me to say things that are not correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to ask the Trial Chamber for assistance to have the witness answer the question and to follow my instructions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, counsel. Witness, the evidence you have given so far about how this statement was recorded and how you were meant to sign sometimes blank sheets has been understood, so please comply with the questions by counsel. Even if he asks you to read the part of the statement which you are contesting, you should just read it. And thereafter, you can answer the questions.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. That's what I will do. So the statement that I provided to the SUP, the last sentence reads: "I did not attend party meetings or pay membership fees." The rest of the statement until the end was added on.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: I asked you to read the last passage of the statement in front of you, the very last one.

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't understand what you are asking me to do.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: The last sentence of this statement.

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of the statement, yes. "I have nothing to add. I have read the statement and have no objections and confirm it with my signature."

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: "And have no objections."

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it's not quite clear here.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Was this statement read to you by the investigator on the occasion that you signed it?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that one part of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: When you signed the statement, were you forced to sign it by the investigator?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Did you provide this statement voluntarily?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: When I say "voluntarily," I mean that he didn't beat, you he didn't threaten you, he didn't make any threats.

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I've already stated today before providing the statement, we were abused.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Please answer my question in the course of questioning.

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: While you were questioned, did the investigator force you to sign blank statements?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Who?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Both Mr. Savic and Mr. Sarkanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Did you sign in the same place?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Did he threaten you?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Did he beat you?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, he did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness please be shown the additional -- or the addition to his statement. This is a statement dated the 21st of October, 1992. It's marked, the English version of the Prosecution, 00697114 and the B/C/S version is marked 00532785.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Can we have the number for identification, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours. It's document D29/3 ID for the English version, and it's D28/3 [sic] ter ID for the B/C/S version.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry. There's been a mistake. It should be 29 ter. I'm sorry. D29 -- it said in the transcript D28/3 ter ID, and it should be 29, I believe.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That's right. It's document D29/3 ID for the English and ter for the B/C/S version. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Dagovic, did you see this addition to the statement?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Is your signature on this statement?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Do you remember when you gave this statement?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Was this at the premises of the Bosanski Samac SUP?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Did this addition to your statement, does it correctly state what you told the investigators?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Do you mean that about the whole statement or only a part of it?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: One part of it, the last part of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: And can you tell us which sentence begins, that part that's not correct, begins with which sentence?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It will be clearer if I give you the last sentence of the part that does state what I said. I would also like to state that I did not participate in any way in the formation of the SDA and the text that follows this sentence, I am not familiar with.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Could you please read the last sentence of this statement.

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "I have nothing more to say. I do not wish to read the statement and confirm it with my signature."

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Was this statement read out to you?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, part of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Were you forced to sign this statement?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Do you remember where you placed your signature?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I can see, down there on the left-hand side.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: In the middle of the page?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the left-hand side.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: No. I am speaking about the length of the text. So sort of around the middle.

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Were you told to sign it there?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Was it entered there, the statement made by?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Probably since I signed it there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Do you remember whether there was any empty space between your signature and the text that was typewritten?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Was -- is it possible that there was no empty space? Perhaps you did not hear the entire statement?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Maybe yes, maybe no.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Counsel, do you think you could find out from the witness how many blanks he thinks or recalls that he signed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: You heard Judge Williams. How many blank papers did you sign?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I can remember, I signed three statements, written statements, that is, and three blank pieces of paper.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Were you told where you were supposed to place your signature on these blank sheets of paper that you signed?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Where?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was either on the left or on the right. But every time I was told "sign here," and that's where I signed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Can we agree that this is not these two statements that you signed as blank sheets of paper. These statements are not the blank sheets you signed?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: There is no stamp of the MUP on these statements.

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I can see, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: As far as you know, they weren't placed on other statements either?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, they weren't.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Just one more question. Did you place your signature at the bottom of the page every time?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I can't exactly remember. You can ask me, but ...

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Dagovic, now I would like to take you back to a different subject. I would like to put a few questions to you about that. And that is your exchange. You were exchanged in Dragalic in November 1992; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: As you were going to the place of exchange, you were checked by the members of the UN forces, or to be precise, the members of the Nepalese battalion; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What do you mean checked?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: I mean they let you pass. You passed their check point; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: When you were exchanged, were representatives of the International Community present, the Red Cross, the OSC, the so-called monitors, the European Union et cetera?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Probably, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: And you wanted to be exchanged; right?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was forced to be exchanged.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: I'm asking you whether you wanted to be exchanged.

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I did not want to be exchanged and I didn't want to go to the camp either.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Did any of the representatives of the International Community ask you whether you wanted to be exchanged and did you answer them that you did not want to be exchanged?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Nobody asked us a thing.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Nobody addressed you at all?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. This was just a group exchange. Such and such a number of people for such and such a number of people.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: That is to say that you saw people who had come from the other side.

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, they sat in our buses. They boarded our buses. I saw that. And we boarded their buses.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: It was roughly the same number?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Perhaps there were even more. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. The next counsel. Mr. Lazarevic, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, on behalf of Mr. Zaric's defence, I will conduct the cross-examination of this witness. But if you could bear just one second until I can prepare all my questioning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Mr. Dagovic. I'm Alexander Lazarevic, attorney at law. You have probably heard already that I will be conducting your cross-examination for the defence of Simo Zaric. My colleague, Mr. Krgovic, already said to you what we usually say to all witnesses testifying here. So please don't misunderstand me. These proceedings are being interpreted. So we try to make an effort to slow down. So when I complete my question, I wait for your answer. You will see that the question has been recorded in the transcript, and then you can give me your answer. I really made an effort to prepare very simple questions that require simple yes/no answers. So what you do not say, please tell me -- so what you do not understand, please tell me. Also, if you do not understand something that I'm asking, just tell me that you do not understand, and then I'll do my best to rephrase my question, and try to clarify this question, then. Before I start putting questions to you, on behalf of my client, I would like to say to you that he is truly sorry for the suffering that you personally and your family went through during this war. Since he is still not in a position to say anything here, he asked me to convey this to you. So if you don't mind, I would like to start with the cross-examination now.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note. Could counsel please speak into the microphone. We have great difficulty hearing him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Counsel, if you can move closer to the microphone.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I will try to place the microphone in the right site.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Dagovic, while testifying here, you said a few things to us. I shall go into some matters that we did not perhaps tackle in sufficient detail. You said to us that you were employed by the Bicic brothers in their pizzeria. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Can you please tell me what your working hours were while you were employed at the Bicic brothers' pizzeria. I mean, did you work every day? Did you work Saturdays? Sundays? Until when did you work in the evening? How long would you stay on perhaps after the pizzeria would close?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That would depend on the customers. I mean, how many customers there were. If there were more customers, then we'd have to stay on and work longer. If there were less, then it would be different. But in principle, we hardly ever closed before, say, 12.00. And I also worked in shifts, so sometimes I would work in the first shift, sometimes I would work in the second shift. It depend. I would also work weekends.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: So the pizzeria worked on Saturdays and Sundays also.

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You said to us while you were testifying here that you were a member of the SDA. I'm going to put a question to you now, although I think that today during your cross-examination by my colleague Mr. Krgovic, you did indicate to us some things that I would like to ask you about. Are you aware of the existence of certain SDA patrols that patrolled the town of Samac at the beginning of 1992 until the conflict broke out on the 16th of April? Are you aware of that fact?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know, it is true that there were some. But I don't know what you mean by "patrols." If somebody just drove around in a car unarmed, I wouldn't call that a patrol.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Well, I don't want to go into all of that now, to qualify it this way or that way. Let's put it some other way now.
