Do you know whether some members of the SDA went around town during the night with a certain task to see whether there was anything unusual going on, whether there were any movements that were unusual in town? Let me rephrase the question that way, then.

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I assume, then that, you did not participate in any such activities.

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Since I worked, I had very little time to participate in any such thing.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes. That's what I assumed. I said that you had practically indicated what your answer to this question would be, but I am putting the question to you now, nevertheless. Now I would like to move on to April 17th. The early morning hours of the 17th of April. In your statement, you said that this was around 2.00 or 3.00 a.m., so this was practically the night during the 16th or 17th. Nevertheless, it was after midnight. And then you said that you saw military vehicles when you went out as they were moving in all directions; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. But this pertained not only to that night but to previous nights as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: If I understand your answer correctly, there were some movements by military vehicles during the night, even before that night between the 16th and 17th of April.

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. By day and by night.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Now I would like to concentrate precisely on April 17th, if that's not a problem, and these military vehicles that you mentioned, then. Can you tell me specifically what kind of vehicles these were. You know what I mean, whether these were passenger vehicles, jeeps, tanks, guns.

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I mean pinzgauers, or shall I call them jeeps, and there were also trucks. That is to say, no passenger vehicles.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell me specifically. We are talking about the early morning hours of the 17th all the time. How many such vehicles did you see?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know the exact number. I only saw them. I did not count them.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: On that occasion, did you perhaps see some soldiers or only the vehicles as they were moving?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I saw vehicles. And now, what was in the vehicles, behind, I really don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I understand. So outside the vehicles, there weren't any soldiers.

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean that night? You mean that night?

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes. We're talking about that night all the time.

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I only saw these vehicles.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: You stated that after that, you returned to your home. Can you tell us when you returned approximately to your home in relation to when you went out. You said it was 2.00 or 3.00 a.m.

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not actually go out into town. I went out into the yard. So basically, I was at home, but I was in the yard of my house. So perhaps this could have been a few minutes, not longer than that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: So practically you went out only for a few minutes to the gate, and you returned.

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, you could put it that way.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: And then perhaps -- yes, again, we are talking about the same day and the same date. Did you see anybody or anything else on the streets, except for those military vehicles you mentioned. You said there were no soldiers, but was there anybody else?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Let me tell you. When I saw these vehicle, I heard voices, and I saw somebody running up. At that time, I saw a neighbour of mine, which surprised me. He was a good friend of mine. So I saw movements by persons, but these were not large groups of people. Later on, it turned out that inter alia this friend of mine was a member of the 4th Detachment.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: As for this subject, the 4th Detachment, we'll get to that later. But I was just interested in this particular context now. That night had passed and then the day of the 17th of April came. According to your statement, you said that after break breakfast, together with Hasan Bicic, you went to the pizzeria. Is that the way it was? You had breakfast and after that, you went with Hasan Bicic?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell me to the best of your recollection what time this was approximately when you set out for the pizzeria.

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I can't remember the exact time. But I know it was in the morning. If I were to say that it was 9.00 or 10.00, perhaps I would be telling a lie. Perhaps it was 10.30, perhaps it was 7.30.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: As far as you can remember.

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know really.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: On that occasion, when you set out for the pizzeria together with Hasan Bicic, did you notice that Hasan Bicic had some weapon with him?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know whether he had a weapon, but since he had a pistol and he had a licence for that pistol, perhaps he had that pistol.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: You don't know, but you do not reject the possibility of him having had a weapon.

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. Maybe he did.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell me what Hasan was wearing on that occasion. Did he perhaps wear a uniform or a hunting vest or something like that, if you recall?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: To be quite frank, I can't remember really. I think he wore his leather jacket with a Top Gun emblem on it. But I really can't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: To the best of your recollection, a leather -- a leather jacket with some emblems.

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not some emblems. A Top Gun emblem.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Oh, I see, a Top Gun emblem. You said to us that at that time you were very close, very friendly with Hasan Bicic and Muhamed Bicic, and you were practically like brothers, your brother and you and they. Is that correct? I'm talking about that period of time. I don't know whether you can say that of the present time as well, but we're talking about that time.

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Counsel, could you clarify with the witness what a Top Gun emblem is, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Your Honour. I'm familiar with this insignia, and I thought that everyone is, but --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: I apologise. But frankly, I'm not.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I will definitely ask the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Dagovic, as you see, Judge Williams would like to know what a Top Gun emblem is. So could you explain this a bit more precisely for this Court.

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was a famous movie starring Tom Cruise, and it was called Top Gun, and these jackets were very fashionable then. So he wore that kind of jacket.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Can we say that this is a jacket that is supposed to look like a jacket worn by US airmen?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wouldn't put it that way. It was just a movie. Well, possibly. Perhaps I could agree with you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Is this okay with --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: I am perfectly satisfied. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Sir, we talked about your relationship with the Bicic brothers now, and we said how close you were to them. I have a question for you in this connection. We have some information about this already, but I'm asking you about what you know. Do you know that Hasan Bicic had an automatic rifle, a Kalashnikov?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know, no. But I know that he had an automatic pistol. This new 1999-type, so it could fire a burst of gunfire. But you said a Kalashnikov. No.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: So you don't know that he had a Kalashnikov. Do you know whether his brother, Muhamed Bicic perhaps had a Kalashnikov also? We know that he had a hunting weapon, but I'm asking about the Kalashnikov.

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: That day, the 17th of April, on that day either on your own or together with Hasan Bicic, were you in the park, in the centre of town? You know which park I'm referring to, the park in the centre of Samac.

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: And as you went to the pizzeria -- when you went after breakfast to the pizzeria, you had breakfast with Bicic, and then you went to the pizzeria. As you were walking, did you see any members of the SDA in town then perhaps?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember having seen anyone then.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: We questioned a number of witnesses here with regard to certain circumstances. I'm going to put some questions to you now. And of course, if you don't know, just tell me you don't know. On that occasion, did you perhaps see Ibrahim Salkic, nicknamed Ibela, armed?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not see him then, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I can infer from your answer that you perhaps saw him those days. But could you tell us for the transcript when did you see him? A day earlier? A day later?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I saw him later, but I did not see that he was armed. Perhaps he had something underneath his jacket, but ...

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: When you say "later," are you referring to the 18th, the next day?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, maybe the day after that too. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Did you perhaps see Izet Izetbegovic armed?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Did you see a certain Ivica Djebic, nicknamed Crv, did you see him armed on that day, the 17th?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I saw Ivica Djebic, but I did not see him armed. He was just crying because they had killed his brother, but I didn't see any weapons.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Can you just tell me where you saw him, Ivica Djebic, on that occasion, that is to say, on the 17th.

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember, but I know that it was between my house and the pizzeria -- rather, between the pizzeria to my house.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: At the time that you were going towards the pizzeria together with Hasan Bicic, was there any shooting in the town? Did you hear shooting? 12 page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. Were bullets flying? Was there any fighting on streets?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did hear shooting, but I don't know whether this was fighting. But when I did go to the camp, I saw that there was often shooting in front of the SUP.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Well, here I'm specifically interested on the 17th, when you were going to the pizzeria, was there any shooting then?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Shooting was coming from the direction of the SUP, but I don't know who was shooting or what was going on.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Well, I'm only interested in the fact that there was some shooting. There was shooting; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: And let me ask you, when you arrived there, was the pizzeria damaged? Were there any signs of fighting or signs of battle that were visible on the pizzeria itself?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That time, that morning, there were none. But after that, after, there were.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Did you see on the day of the 17th any kind of fighting in Samac?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Like I just told you, I did hear shooting, but I don't know who was shooting at whom.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I'm just asking did you see any shooting.

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: And that part of town, around the pizzeria where the park is and the bank, that section of the town of Samac, did you see any armed people there that day?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Your brother, did he leave the house at all that day, if you know? And if he did, where did he go?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. He went to the pizzeria together with Hasan and me.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: So the three of you went together.

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Muhamed was also there because the pizzeria is about 60 metres away from their house. I can't remember all the details right now, whether he entered the pizzeria, whether he went back, or whether he was just in front of the pizzeria, but I know that he was with us.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: In the course of this conversation, we just mentioned Muhamed and Hasan Bicic. So I just wanted to ask you something about their families. Were they in Samac at that time?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Do you know perhaps when they left Samac, the families of Hasan and Muhamed Bicic?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They left immediately before the outbreak of the war. But I don't know exactly when.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Can you please tell me, the night between the 17th and the 18th, where were you?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the basement.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Of your house, or were you in some other basement? We have to clarify that.

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the basement, or in the cellar of my house.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Was anyone else with you there at that time, in the cellar?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: My uncle, my brother's -- my father's brother was there as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: And your brother, your mother, your father, were they there as well?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I meant that together with all of us, he was there too.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I think that it's all clear for the transcript now, Witness.

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. You're right.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Now I would like to move to the 18th of April. If I understood your statement correctly - because sometimes some dates or some things have been recorded in an unclear way - so the 18th is the day that the army came in front of your house to collect weapons. Was that on the 18th?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I wouldn't agree with you, because I think I stated in that statement that this happened during those two days. Perhaps it was the 18th or the 19th or even the 20th. But it happened during those couple of days.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Well, we've had two dates here that were mentioned by witnesses who have been questioned so far. So perhaps we could try to establish the correct date. I assume that your answer suggests that you don't know that this was perhaps on the 19th. What I'm interested in is to know whether this was on the 17th. Was that on the day that you went to the pizzeria with the Bicic brothers?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that this was not on the 17th. But weapons were collected over several days. And if I may be allowed to add, it was announced on the radio that weapons should be taken out onto the streets and that vehicles will be coming by to collect those weapons, and if some people -- and then that's what happened, people placed the weapons outside, and then members of the 4th Detachment came, and they collected the weapons.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: So if I've understood you properly, it was not on the 17th that all this happened. Could you please tell me the approximate time when the army arrived in front of your house, as far as you can recollect. What time did they arrive at your house?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If I'm not mistaken, it was in the morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, I would like now to offer one photograph. This is the photograph of the house of Mr. Esad Dagovic. I would like to have an ID number for it so far. This photograph --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: When was it taken? When was it taken?

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: This photograph was taken during this recess. So it has been taken maybe some ten days ago. And we brought them with us when we arrived in The Hague. I multiplied these photographs, and I already gave copies to our colleagues from the Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Weiner.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: If it's a fair and accurate representation of what the house looked like in 1992 according to the witness, that's fine.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Anyway, you have a copy of the photograph. Yes, it can be shown to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Of course I will wait for the witness to confirm or to deny that this is this picture, and then I will ask it to be tendered into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Your Honour, we have several photographs here. It looks like four.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Okay. The usher will show you which one, so you'll see whether or not you have a similar copy.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, I believe that it would be in the best interest of the defendants that we put this photograph on the ELMO so they can see what --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Can you just wait a minute. Has the Prosecutor seen the copy that the witness is looking at?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Just a moment, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Can we have an ID number, please, a number for identification.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours. It's D15/4 ID.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Counsel, you can go ahead and ask the witness your questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Dagovic, the question is very simple: Is this your house in Samac?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: In April 1992, it was there in the same place and nothing has changed since then in this regard.

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's true, except it was in much better condition.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Probably.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: The witness has identified this photograph as a photograph of his house and also confirmed that during 1992, this photograph -- this house was also in the same position. I would like to tender it into evidence, instead of ID number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Any objection, Mr. Weiner?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: No objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: I take it it will retain the same number?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: So it will be Exhibit D15/4.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That's right. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: You said that it was in a better condition, but I wanted to ask you: Was it in -- was the facade in this same state, or was the facade ever finished?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. It was never finished completely. So basically, it had drainpipes, but -- which are not there any more. But it was more or less in the same state on the outside as it is now.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Dagovic, if I'm not mistaken, your house is in a yard. It's inside, situated inside a yard; is this correct?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's true. And it has a view out on to the street.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, now I would like to offer another photograph. It's also a photograph that was already given to the -- my colleagues from the OTP. And this is also taken during the recess -- all the four photographs that I have have the same story, actually.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: And it is a photograph of what?

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: This is a photograph of the front house, I believe. Of course I'll have to wait the witness to confirm that. And this is actually his uncle's or his father's brother's house, that runs the street.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: All right. Yes. Can they be shown to the witness, and can we have copies.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Weiner.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: We might want to save time. We might not even have to place an ID number on the photographs now and just see if the witness indicates they are a fair and accurate representation, we can just give it a straight evidentiary number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: All right. Can we just -- yes. Can we see them. Yes, counsel, you can go ahead with your questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Dagovic, is this your uncle's house?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: In 1992, it was in the same place where it is today.

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Can we have an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours. It's Exhibit D16/4.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SINGH
utterances.text: Sorry, Mr. Lazarevic, you mean in the same state or the same place? I mean, the house has got to be in the same place.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Well, I understand Your Honour's concern in this regard, but this is not always necessary. And my next line of questioning will show why am I referring to that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Dagovic, this photograph of your uncle's house, can we agree that your uncle's house is practically one that faces the street, that looks out directly onto the street?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, we cannot agree on that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: On this picture, I see the street, and I don't see any other building between the street and the house. And this is why I'm asking you whether that house faces directly onto the street.

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You've taken a nice photograph of the picture from only one side. But I can provide the Chamber with another photograph where you can see that my house -- my house from another angle. So my house is here, in this area, and it also faces the street, because what you're trying to say is that this house is in front of my house, but you can see that behind this house, there isn't another house. My house is here, next to this house, and it's visible. The windows are looking out on to the street.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes. To offer perhaps to the witness to make at least once sketch of this yard and the house where his house was located and where his uncle's house was located, so we could maybe understand better the position of this house.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Okay. I think the other problem is when you say the house faces the street, the impression I have normally would be the front door of the house looks on to the street. Now, when I look at this house, I can't see a door. I can see only windows. Maybe that's where the problem is also.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SINGH
utterances.text: I think perhaps you may want to suggest to him that the house abuts on the street, abuts.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Maybe that's the better expression. I thank you Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: So you want the witness to draw -- to have a sketch?

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Well, if it doesn't give him a problem.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: If he can.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Dagovic, you were about to explain that to us. So if these photographs do not indicate the situation in the best possible way, could you please then sketch that on the piece of paper. So if you can sketch the plot, and then sketch your house and your uncle's house, so that we would get a true picture. Is that a problem for you?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I will do that, in any case, but I would also like to suggest to the Trial Chamber that I provide photographs where you can see the view from my windows on to the street and the view from the street of my house, because they show different angles.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: As far as I know, you are not in a position to personally submit evidence before this Chamber. This is something that is up to the Prosecution, so they're the only ones who can do that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Mr. Lazarevic, I'm just a little bit puzzled as to where we're going with this line of questioning. Is it -- what's the relevance as to whether a house is looking on to the street and this and that? I mean, I -- I'm just puzzled.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Well, Your Honours, if you don't this mind, during this line of examination, after showing two more photographs, I will go with this line of examination, it has something to do about the arrival of the army and the moment when he could possibly see that and ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I will sketch to the best of my ability, and if necessary, I can also provide photographs indicating the different position.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Could you now, please, mark with the letter "A" the house of your uncle and with the letter "B" your house.

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, may the record reflect that the witness indicated with letter "A" the position of his house and with letter -- of his uncle's house, sorry, and with letter "B" his own house.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: If I might have a number for this because I would like to tender it into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: There is nothing else you want him to discuss on this sketch, before we -- because it has to be handed to the registry assistant.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: You are through with the sketch?

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I believe that I already said everything. But maybe if only -- or if we could have some indication about how far from the beginning of the street and how deep in this space is his own house located.

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: About 10 metres from the street, at the most.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I have no other questions in regard to this sheet that the witness --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Can the witness indicate with the letter "C" where the street is, because I can't -- I don't understand Serbo-Croat, but I can see the same writing in two places.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes, it is in B/C/S. Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Okay. So that's where the street is, and he has said his house is about 10 metres away.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: We don't have a number for this sheet.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. So can we have the sketch given to the registry.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Can we have the sketch given to the registry assistant, for purposes of marking it. I believe the Prosecution has no objection to having it entered into evidence?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Yes. No objection. No objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: All right. Can we have the exhibit number, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours. It's Exhibit D17/4.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Dagovic, could you please look at the previous photograph, D16/4, and use the pointer to show us on the right side, if I understood you properly, there is a fence there; isn't that right? And according to your sketch, this is where your house should be. So please, could you show that to us.

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. You are right. My house is right here, in between. This is the fence from my uncle's house. This is my fence. This is the entrance to my house, which goes behind this house. And this is where my house was, right here. And it was facing the street. So between this house and the other house was my house. There was a house there, which has been knocked down now, and you can see the fence and the end of the yard, and this is where my house was, which faced the street.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: This house that was demolished, that used to stand there, this is what I wanted to ask you about. There, on the right side, can you confirm that there was a house there once, a house owned by Anto Bauman, and this house no longer stands there.

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The house did not belong to Bauman, Anto. It belonged to Lovro. And before that, it belonged to my grandfather who sold it to Lovro and his wife.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: So now, we're talking about 1992. And that house was still standing right there.

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, you are right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Although we have only a photograph, maybe on the photograph itself the witness can mark with a red mark an "X" where the house which is now demolished used to be, to clear the record. Yes, Mr. Weiner.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Your Honour, they took these photographs, and it seems take took photographs from every angle but from the street into that house. And I was just wondering, do they have a photograph of what would have been the proper picture to take, and if they do --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Because the counsel said they took the photographs during the recess, that is December/January.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And it's of an angle straight on to the uncle's house, to the left of the uncle's house. But they didn't stake a picture from the street to the right of the uncle's house, which is where this witness's house is. And I was wondering, do they have one, which would make things much easier.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: I'm sure counsel can answer that. Mr. Lazarevic?

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, our investigator did the best they could. They didn't have some sort of instructions from us from this angle, from this angle, or another angle. We just wanted them to photograph the situation that is now. As soon as we got these photographs, they told us that they know that there was a certain house that was -- that existed in 1992, but now it's destroyed, and so this is the fact that I asked the witness about. Unfortunately, I cannot have a picture made in 1992 to show this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: It's all right.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: And for this reason.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. I don't think there is much of a problem, because on D16/4, beside the uncle's house where he indicated the fence, and he did point with a pointer on the ELMO where the house used to be, which has since been demolished. That's when I said they can just mark on the photograph where the house used to be with an "X."

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: That's what I thought also.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Lazarevic, going back to the question I raised as to relevance, and you indicated what it was, whether the house of the witness whether there would be a view of the street and the vehicles and so on. So thinking of what Mr. Weiner has just said, I mean, you probably can't see very clearly me holding the photograph up here, but one would have thought your photographer would have not only stood on the street and taken it from that angle, but would have walked up the street and taken the photograph looking in through the gap.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, we have two more photographs that we believe will show exactly what is the position of this house, looking from the street. Because these are photographs of the crossroads that is near the street and exactly shows --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Can they be shown to the witness. Perhaps they will clear the picture.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes, they will be shown to the witness, and he will indicate. Yes. Of course I will do that, but Your Honour, you already have ordered the witness to point --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: No. Maybe it won't be necessary if those photographs are showed -- if the photographs you have are shown to the witness. Maybe it won't be necessary. May I ask, Mr. Lazarevic, I'm wondering also, following on Judge Williams' question, are you disputing his evidence that he saw army vehicles on that evening?

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: No, Your Honour. This is not the question about the early morning of 17 of April. It --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. What is it going to? What is the relevance? Maybe you should explain.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: On 18, or maybe 19.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: What?

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: On 18 or maybe 19 of April, the army came in front of his house to collect weapons. And this is what we are talking about now. And there are some facts that I actually was speaking about with my client, and he informed me about some things that he doesn't find that were exact. And so for this reason, I want to challenge this -- this part of testimony.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Weiner. You are on your feet.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: I was just going to say these are two more pictures from the left -- to the left. And not only to the left but almost angular to the left that, it still doesn't offer us any help. Because the picture we need is from the house -- from actually just of the right of the father -- the uncle's house inside, towards this gentleman's home.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: The witness's house.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SINGH
utterances.text: Mr. Lazarevic, I think -- the witness --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, would you let me say something?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SINGH
utterances.text: Well, no, the witness says that he has a picture that can help. I mean, if he says that that's his house, maybe you will want to wish -- you may wish to look at it at least, and then make a decision. If it can help quickly, then all right.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Of course, Your Honour. I will definitely take it into consideration if this is it is. But what I would suggest is we don't have pictures from 1992, of course unless the witness has it with him, and I would be glad to check it with him and with the Prosecutors, with my colleagues, to see if this is a photograph from 1992. I don't believe that we can make it better than this --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Because we are wasting a lot of time. The witness wanted to say something. What did you want to say?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I thank you for letting me speak. Since these photographs were made from angles that are agreeable to these gentlemen, I have pre-war, war and post-war photographs where you can see quite clearly. I know what the gentleman is trying to say, that they could not see the soldiers as they came. They came to my house, gentlemen. They came here, Mr. Zaric and Tadic were there. And now this side you can see it here, you can see the fence of my neighbour. If you look in the direction of my yard, you can see this empty space. So I could see them from this side too. I could see them from the side of my yard, or rather, the entrance, and I could also see them through the window of my house, or rather, our yard. This was our yard. We were in one yard. So if you allow me, I am going to submit to you my photographs where you can see the house from all angles, and I also have a video cassette. Perhaps that will facilitate matters. This picture was taken from a different street.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Weiner.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: I was just going to say, it's not redirect examination, but I just would like -- if the Court could ask the witness, does he have these in his possession at this time, or are these at his home.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Because I was about to say, we would like to establish the truth.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. We would like to have our hands on any evidence that would assist us in establishing the truth. So I'll find out from the witness. Witness, you do say you have photographs which can eliminate these problems we are facing right now. You also have video footage. Do you have them with you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Unfortunately I don't have them here with me. But I can make sure that you get them within two days, and then everything can be seen quite clearly from that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Maybe we can leave this part of the cross-examination, then you can move on to other parts, then you come back to it when we have the clear photographs.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. With your instruction, I will follow that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SINGH
utterances.text: Mr. Lazarevic, the other thing was that I think in his examination-in-chief he said he was outside in the yard when the tank and the soldiers came. So I think the question here is if he was in the yard, then was the yard in front of this road. In other words, you could still see straight ahead. Although you may not be able to see from the house, was he able to see from the yard where he says he was. I think that is the contextual situation, and not where the house is.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Your Honour is completely right, and if I may add, so far I didn't pose him a question about this -- about this. I mean, I didn't ask him whether he was in the house. He already stated that he was in the yard. I just wanted to show the situation that was at that time in this yard, regarding where the house is, and then I wanted to ask him where were you in the yard, because you already stated that you were in the yard. And to establish where, exactly, he was in position. How far he was in position to see the military vehicles that was approaching his house.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SINGH
utterances.text: But I think when you hear military vehicles like tanks coming, you can even hear the rumble before it arrives.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes. That's --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Maybe you can move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I will continue, and we will deal with this later, I believe.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. So these two photographs on the ELMO right now --

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: If it is easier --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: We might not use them --

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: We might mark them just for ID, or whatever it is decision of Court, I will agree with it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. We could mark them.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Perhaps --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: They can also be produced. But they don't solve the problem, anyway. It's just that they were discussed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Whatever Your Honour pleases.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Can I have the numbers, exhibit numbers for the two of them.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours. Exhibit numbers D18/4 and D19/4.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: We shall now continue, and then, depending on how the Trial Chamber rules, we may go back to this subject.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... of these last two, D18 and D19, so that we all mark them correctly.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: May I proceed, Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. I think you can proceed. We'll get them later.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Dagovic, during your testimony, you said that a tank came in front of your house, and that Mr. Zaric and that Mr. Tadic were there in front of your house, standing on that tank. While you were being examined by the Prosecutor, you stated that you had done your military service. So I would like to put a few questions to you in this regard. Do you know what a Praga is?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Could you please tell the Court, then. It's been mentioned several times here, and we haven't fully clarified it. What is a Praga exactly?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: A Praga is an anti-aircraft gun. This was not that. This looked like a vehicle, like a truck. If you think that I have confused a Praga and a tank, that's not the case.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: That's what I wanted to ask you, but I see that you have already responded. So let me just ask you one more thing. Do you know what a BOV is?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Was it perhaps a BOV?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. A BOV is a combat armoured vehicle.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: This military vehicle that came in front of your house was a tank. It wasn't a BOV, it wasn't a Praga. That is your assertion.

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: When you first noticed this tank coming up, how far away was it? When is it that you first saw it from your house?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, perhaps 3 or 4 metres away. If you can give me back the picture of my yard, I can show you this.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Precisely. So it was already --

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In front of the house.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: When you first saw it?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What do you mean "first saw it"?

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I mean in front of your house.

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes, in front of my house, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: At that moment, therefore, the tank stopped in front of your house, and that's the first time you saw Zaric and Tadic standing.

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When the tank stopped, we saw it, and we had heard it, because it was coming from the direction of the pizzeria. And it came to that space, that area that can be seen from my house, on the street. And then it stopped, and then 10 or 20 soldiers walked into the yard, to the best of my assessment, and they asked us to come out. And then when I went out, they asked me to hand over my weapons. And then I saw Mr. Zaric and Mr. Tadic as they were standing on the tank -- on the caterpillars of the tank, because the tank was standing -- and then they also faced -- turned the gun towards the house. The gun was facing the house, or rather, this passage, that is to say, the yard.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: These are not -- these are the details that I'm seeking to clarify. So you see Zaric and Tadic as you were practically getting out in front of your house, out of the yard, when the tank was already standing there.

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. You see, when I got into the yard, I did not go out of the yard. I was in my yard, and this was in front of the yard. So that is three four metres, the street and my yard, and that's when I saw them.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: So that means that they were standing on the caterpillars of the tank, according to what you just said?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This tank was not moving. It was standing.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Did you see the turret of the tank as it was turning or when you first saw it, had it already turned?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It had already turned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SINGH
utterances.text: Mr. Lazarevic, I'm looking at your D18, your D18, perhaps you want to just ask him to mark with some ink the direction from which the tank came and where it went, assuming that we accept this photograph, which I think would be a good representation, because we roughly know where your -- where the gate is and where the uncle's house is, and his house is inside. Right?

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, that was my intention, in regard to that particular photograph.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SINGH
utterances.text: I think if we see all the photographs together, we do understand this.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Following instructions from Judge Mumba and --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SINGH
utterances.text: Yes. We have pieced them together.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, this is the wrong picture. It was coming from the other direction. Could I get a different picture so that I could -- so that I could show it in the empty space by my house? This was wrong. They were coming from this direction here, and not from that direction out there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SINGH
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for Judge Singh, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SINGH
utterances.text: Sorry. You have 17 and 18 there. So you can -- or take all four and just draw the direction, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I wanted to be of assistance, if I may. It is in my opinion D17 which you had in mind, and actually, the witness is asking for the same picture -- D16. I'm sorry. That's the photograph. And the 17 is the sketch. Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 18.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: You have heard the Honourable Judge Singh. Could you just mark the direction from which this vehicle, this tank came?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The tank came from this direction, that is to say, I saw it here, through the window. The tank stopped here in front of my house. It turned its turret, or rather, its gun towards my house. Mr. Zaric was standing here on this side with Mr. Tadic, that is to say, the side facing my yard. I walked out into my yard, so I saw this clearly. So they were coming from this direction. I saw them here and I also -- well, I saw them twice, then.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Can we have the markings. We know that he has explained where the arrow is. He saw the -- the tank first there and then where it has stopped in front of the gate. Can we have it marked some number, counsel, so that we are all clear as to what this diagram on the photograph stands for.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Okay. May I suggest what -- this is the photograph of witness's house --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: No. It has an identification number, I think. It's D --

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: D16/4, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. It's D16/4. So we just want this -- the marking he has made for the tanker facing his house to be either 1 or 2 or whatever.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SINGH
utterances.text: And just to make things further clearer, if you look at B -- D15, that little, that white wall at the right side, is that part of your uncle's house, which can be seen in the photograph you've just marked?

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If you're referring to this, yes, this is part of my uncle's house.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SINGH
utterances.text: Then that is the yard in front of your house, then. In the photo on the ELMO. Right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. But it was one yard. All this was one yard. You see? You see, this is a free passageway here. All of this was one yard. And please may attention to this. You can see the light here in relation to this. So the house only concealed part of my house. So the light came clearly from the street. There was not a house in front.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Can we then have the house which you've pointed at as your uncle's marked with the letter "X", please, so that is clear, on the photograph which is now on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes, on this photograph that is now on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Dagovic, you heard the Trial Chamber. They're asking you to mark your uncle's house with number "1" -- no the photograph that you're watching now.

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This one?

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes, this one.

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: So part of the house.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes, the part of the house that you can see.

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. That makes it clearer now because as you explained -- we can see where the shadow is falling and we can see the other part of your house where there's no shadow.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Can we see the other photograph where you drew this -- the photograph where you drew the sketch of the tanker, or whatever you call it. Yes, can we have it marked?

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes. The photograph of Mr. Dagovic's uncle's house --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: It has an identification number. I just wanted --

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Okay. With the arrow showing the direction --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: And then where he drew this figure.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Where the tank came from.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mm-hm.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: And together with the picture.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Where the tank stopped.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: The shadow of the tank on the left side.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: In front of the gate. Can we have it marked "X." Because when you look at the photograph and you're reading the transcript, then you'll be wondering what this is. If it's marked "X," then you can tell that this is where the tanker stopped, as drawn on the photograph.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: At this moment, Your Honour, I don't believe I follow exactly what you mean.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: You see the photograph on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I'll ask for the help of my colleagues to ... Yes, okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Dagovic, can you mark your uncle's house by number "1."

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I already explained that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: On this picture, in order to be able to identify it in the transcript.

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Since this picture is already number "1," can I put number "2"?

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: No. They differ between themselves.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... so just put "1" there, on the picture on the screen right now. Yes, it's the same house. Can you ask him also to mark the tanker he had drawn? Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Well, number "2," with the arrow, I believe that he pointed, and with number "3," the tank.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. To make a distinction, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: So please, the arrow with number "2" and with number "3," the tank that you drew.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. That's better.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Dagovic, so this is the first time you see Tadic and Zaric. When you came to this spot that you already pointed out to us by the gate. You see the two of them; right?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I got out of the house, when I went into the yard, you can see it better here, sir. You see? You took a picture of the yard from this road. You took a picture of the house from here. So you can see this. This is where I went out. And that's where I saw them.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes, that's what I meant?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The house is perhaps 7 metres by 10 metres. Yes, so say from here, it's 7 metres to the corner of the house.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: So therefore, you did not see when the turret was actually turning. It had already been turned when you saw it.

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right. Otherwise, it could not drive on. It would break down all the trees.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I didn't find that clear either. That's why I'm asking you. Mr. Dagovic, you have already testified here before the Tribunal, and you said that you had had a pistol, for which you had a permit. And you wore it out of fear that somebody might steal the money you were carrying from the pizzeria, the earnings of a particular day; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Furthermore, you said -- I mean, we are talking about this situation concerning weapons now. You said that you hid that pistol in the cellar; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: You had a permit for that pistol.

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: We heard from you that over the radio, they were asking citizens to leave weapons in yards and the street, but you did not do that.

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not do that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us more specifically where you hid this pistol in the cellar. Do you remember where it was exactly?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I remember where I hid it. I hid it behind the old washing machine in the cellar. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: In the cellar of your house, underneath the coal, did you have a hidden Kalashnikov?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Underneath the coal? No.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: And in some other place?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Did you have a hidden zolja?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: So it is not correct that you handed over a Kalashnikov in the cellar of your house to Goran Buzakovic?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I handed over to Goran Buzakovic this pistol.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Only the pistol?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He entered the cellar with me, and I handed it over to him. And I remember I showed him so that he could see that the pistol had not been fired at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I was interested in the Kalashnikov and in the zolja specifically. Perhaps -- I beg your pardon -- for the Trial Chamber - I did not look at the transcript - but let us explain what a zolja is so that we would not have to deal with this through another witness.

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I will explain this, but I don't want there to be any misunderstanding that I had this zolja.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: No, no, no.

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know from the army that zolja is an anti-armour weapon, a rocket launcher. How should I explain this to the court. And I didn't have this. Imagine if everybody had that many weapons, as you've been saying or as people could be saying. We could have defended ourselves. We would not be hiding in cellars.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Was your cellar searched after you handed over this weapon?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: On that occasion or some other occasion?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On that occasion.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Now I would like to move on to another subject in connection with this. Of course all of this is interconnected. But now let us leave this aside -- I mean, the weapon-taking. Now we are going to talk about the 4th Detachment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SINGH
utterances.text: Mr. Lazarevic, are you abandoning this -- weapons now? Are you abandoning this point?

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: So far, because -- yes, yes, in so far. But I cannot promise that I will not be back on this in later course. I just want to confer later with my co-counsel. And since we have just five minutes of trial hours today, I would like to do as much as I can for today.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Dagovic, I have carefully read the transcript of your statement. You spoke of the 4th Detachment on several occasions, and you said "Simo's detachment," "Zaric's army," and the like.

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Did you use these terms because in your opinion, Simo Zaric was the commander of this detachment? Was that the reason why you were using precisely these terms?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Zaric on paper was not the commander. It was Radovan Antic. But Mr. Zaric held all the strings. And I saw Mr. Zaric at the police station too, not Radovan Antic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I asked you this because I wanted to know why you had been using precisely this term. If Radovan Antic had been the commander, would you have said "Radovan's army"?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If Radovan had been in charge of the 4th Detachment, I would have said "Radovan's army."

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Do you know --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Counsel, you are forgetting to pause, both of you. Yes. It's difficult for the interpreters.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes. I thought I was slowing down.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So you know that, as you had put it on paper, Radovan Antic was commander of the 4th Detachment.

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Do you know what Jovo Savic was?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not aware of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Speaking further on about the members of the 4th Detachment, can you say about each and every one of them this man was a member of the 4th Detachment, this man was not?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that I could say who the members of the 4th Detachment were. I'm not claiming that I could name all of them, though.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Were there members of the 4th Detachment who were not from the town of Samac?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. There were some people from villages whom I did not know. Perhaps I did know them, since I worked in the pizzeria where people came.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: My colleague already asked you something about this. Did the members of the 4th Detachment -- I mean, I'm talking from -- about the period from the 17th in the morning onwards. Were they wearing white ribbons on their shoulders? Did you see them with white ribbons on their shoulders?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is true that they had them, but I'm not clear what you said. Did you mean the arm or the shoulder?

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I meant shoulder.

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: But they differed from the armbands that were worn by civilians.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I asked you about the white ribbon that many people have confirmed were worn on shoulders, so this is not really ... You mentioned in your statement Dr. Mirko Sisic who you said was a good man and who helped you, who was good and fair to you as a doctor when you came to hospital. Do you know that he was a member of the 4th Detachment?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. But as far as I know, he was there as a doctor, not as a soldier, like his brother was, for example.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I asked you whether he was a member.

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I heard you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: So his brother, Vlado Sisic, he was also a member of the 4th Detachment?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. He was much worse than his brother. Actually, his brother was nice.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Do you know until when the 4th Detachment existed, or rather, when it ceased to exist? Let me rephrase the question that way.

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know about that. But I know that in the time of camps and deportations, the 4th Detachment did exist. About later, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I'm going to put a question to you, and tell me if you don't know. Do you know that the 4th Detachment was disbanded on the 12th of May, 1992, when the 4th Unit of the Republika Srpska Army was established, and then the 4th Detachment was no longer in existence?

utterances.speaker: ESAD DAGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Possibly.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, now it's 6.00. Shall we take a recess?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. We'll continue our proceedings tomorrow at 14.15. Yes, Mr. Weiner.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Your Honour, this is the witness that we've had a problem getting here. He waited here four days without getting on the witness stand, and he had a work problem. Could we just -- or could the Court ask the witness what's convenient for him to come back. I don't know -- initially he was told he was going to finish his testimony today. I don't know if he has clothes to stay overnight. I don't know what his situation is. If the Court could inquire of Victims and Witnesses. I don't want to get him fired from his job too, because his boss was notified by Victims and Witnesses that he would finish today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. I thought that would have been verified by the Victims and Witnesses Unit already, because it should have been obvious to the Prosecution that the cross-examination would not finish in half a day.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: We've received three emails in the past five to ten minutes where the Victims and Witnesses Unit is asking us what is going on and if someone could just inquire what his personal schedule is and if necessary, the Victims and Witnesses Unit could notify his employer that there's a problem. Or does he need to go home and obtain these photographs for tomorrow or --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: No, no, no. I don't think the photographs should be the reason. It's the fact that we haven't finished cross-examination. So the Victims -- I wouldn't be able to verify with him, because I don't want him to feel obliged to come, if you have a problem with his employers, that is a matter the Victims and Witnesses Unit should deal with. Because he can come on another day.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: I just -- should we have someone from the Victims and Witnesses Unit speak with him right now or ...?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: No. We can do it this way. We can adjourn and hope that we'll sit tomorrow. If his discussions with the Victims and Witnesses Unit are such that he can -- he can stay on, then he'll continue. If not, then I'm sure there ought to be another witness. By the way, we are not sitting on Friday because of the maintenance people who have to do court maintenance, so we will only sit up to tomorrow this week, Thursday.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Maybe we could -- maybe we can -- I don't know how far anybody from the Victims and Witnesses Unit is.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: They have to be here because they're sending us emails. So someone has to --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: If we could adjourn for maybe five minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Maybe we will stand down for ten minutes and then be able to sort out this problem. Just for ten minutes, yes. --- Break taken at 6.05 p.m.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: The Trial Chamber is going to adjourn. The Trial Chamber is not pleased with the way things are going, because it was obvious to anybody in these proceedings that this witness wasn't going to complete cross-examination and re-examination in one day, and the arrangements for further proceedings with this witness should have been made long before today. We are adjourning, and the proceedings will continue tomorrow at 14.15. We are hoping that one witness or the other will be brought by the Prosecution. The Court will rise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: be reconvened on Thursday, the 14th day of February, 2002, at 2.15 p.m. 19 20 21 22 23 24 25
